transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, to be honest, I'm just so worn out. I guess that's what brought me in. It's gotten to the point where... well, even just walking from the bedroom to the kitchen feels like I've been hauling lumber all day long. 

And the thing is, resting doesn't help at all. I can sit or lie down for hours, but it doesn't give me anything back. I'm just completely drained.
Over this same period when you've been feeling so drained, how has your mood been? Have you been feeling sad, down, or depressed?

Yeah, I have. It's... well, pretty much every morning I wake up with this heavy, hopeless feeling right in my chest. It just weighs on me right from the start of the day. And honestly, some days I just go out and sit in the garage and cry. I don't even know what starts it most of the time, I just... I just feel incredibly down.
Did this fatigue and low mood start suddenly, or did it develop gradually over time? And was there any illness—like a flu, infection, or anything like that—before these feelings began?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. It wasn't like a switch flipped overnight, so... I guess it just kind of crept up on me gradually. It's hard to pinpoint exactly when it got this heavy. 

And no, I wasn't sick before this. I didn't have a flu or an infection or anything like that. Physically, I was fine. It's just... whatever this is.

When you're feeling this exhaustion and fatigue, does it seem to match how sad or depressed you're feeling, or does the tiredness feel like it's out of proportion—like it's much worse than what your mood alone would explain?

I... I don't really know how to answer that. I mean, they both just feel really bad. The tiredness is awful, and the sadness is awful. I haven't really tried to weigh them against each other to see which one is worse. They just both seem to be there all the time.
When you're having these feelings, do you notice any physical symptoms like muscle aches, sore throat, swollen lymph nodes, or headaches that seem to come along with the exhaustion?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I don't have a sore throat or... swollen glands or anything. And no real headaches either. My body just feels heavy, but it's not really muscle aches like when you're sick. It's just... just the exhaustion.
During these times when you're feeling so down and exhausted, do you notice that you're also worrying a lot? And if so, what kinds of things tend to worry you?

I wouldn't say I'm worrying a lot, no. It's not really like anxiety or... or stressing about things going wrong. It's more just this empty feeling. I'm not sitting around worrying about bills or my health or anything specific. It's just... I just feel too tired and down to care about much of anything, to be honest.
Are there activities or things that you used to enjoy doing—hobbies, time with friends or family, things like that—that you've lost interest in or stopped doing because of how you're feeling?

Yeah. Pretty much everything, honestly. I used to look forward to a lot of things... singing in the choir, playing pickup ball, working on cars. I used to love grilling for the family, too. But now, I just can’t make myself care enough to do any of it. I don't show up for things anymore. I don't even have it in me to answer people’s texts when they reach out. I just... I really have no interest in any of it right now.
